title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
summary: Last release added a guard that every setting read with a literal fallback must match the default declared in package.json. It skipped lists, and lists turned out to be where the real divergence was.

highlights.title: One constant per setting
highlights.description: The test source sets had three spellings across eleven call sites, one of them a constant named DEFAULT_TEST_SEGMENTS that was empty. The exclusion list had four.

highlights.title: 29 tests that proved nothing
highlights.description: With the real list in place, the override arrow tests stopped passing: their fixtures had no file path, so the test source filter had never run in any of them.

sections.heading: Fixes
bullets: Every reading of the test source sets and of the exclusion patterns now goes through one constant that matches package.json.
The guard extended to lists and named constants, not only plain values.
No released build changes behaviour: the declared default was already the value in force.
